pages.quiz:
PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Moments and equilibrium? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Moments and equilibrium.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Moments and equilibrium.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Moments and equilibrium.

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Waves? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Waves.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Waves.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Waves.

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy, Work, Power and Machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Energy, Work, Power and Machines.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Moments and equilibrium and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Energy, Work, Power and Machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Waves and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.

2. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.

4. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. D — Glucose and oxygen

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.

8. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

9. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.

10. A — 100 °C

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy, Work, Power and Machines.

12. D — newton (N)

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Moments and equilibrium; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
